summary: Nonisolated nonnormal CE in every dimension over algebraically closed characteristic zero; explicit all-characteristic cusp envelope error <=2/m and char-zero non-FG.
detailedSummary: Numerical-semigroup cusps have identical reduced conductor quotients and a full boundary homeomorphism, including infinite-conductor supports. Smooth source CE gives all continuous signed obstacles in every dimension at exact hypotheses; surfaces work over all fields and Z_p cusp gives a mixed-characteristic case. A cancellation-sensitive ideal sequence proves 2/m all-support canonical error in every dimension/field. In char zero its envelope lies outside the entire finite real raw ideal cone and canonical finite generation fails.
text:
New higher-dimensional nonnormal continuous-envelope sector and explicit quantitative example, using ENTIRE qualified G331 and own n1--n2. Let H be a proper numerical semigroup (a finitely generated additive subsemigroup of the nonnegative integers containing zero with finite complement) and let c be its conductor integer: every integer >=c belongs to H and c-1 does not. For any field k and d>=2, set R_H=k[t^h (h in H),z_1,...,z_(d-1)] localized at the origin, and S=k[t,z_1,...,z_(d-1)] localized there. Both rings are excellent finite-type domains of dimension d. S is finite over R_H since t is integral (some positive t^h lies downstairs), and their fraction fields coincide because gcd(H)=1. S is regular and integrally closed, hence is the normalization. There is just one centre over the origin. Its conductor is exactly t^c S. To verify this on polynomials, all terms of t-degree >=c multiply into the semigroup ring. If a polynomial has a term of degree h<c, multiply by t^(c-1-h); its coefficient of the forbidden degree c-1 remains nonzero. Distinct t-degrees cannot cancel it. Conductor commutes with localization because S/R_H is finite. The reduced conductor quotients are BOTH k[z_1,...,z_(d-1)] at the origin, and their map is the identity.

The infinite-conductor boundary is nonempty: a valuation killing t and centered on the z-ring belongs to it. Thus n2 proves a full boundary homeomorphism including an actual positive-dimensional-support conductor stratum. In characteristic zero over algebraically closed k, the exact smooth source theorem of n1 gives a greatest continuous independently geometric C/D envelope for EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle on EVERY R_H, in EVERY dimension d. Uniform convergence holds in every canonical degree and for every primary gauge. These are nonnormal nonisolated germs: the normalization fails along t=0, a locus of dimension d-1, because t remains integral but missing at its generic point. The result goes beyond normal smooth finite quotients; it is not inferred from characteristic-zero resolution of these singular germs.

For d=2 the source is a normal surface, so the same all-continuous-obstacle theorem holds over EVERY field, including imperfect fields and positive characteristic. There is also a mixed-characteristic example R=Z_p[[t^2,t^3]]=Z_p[[a,b]]/(b^2-a^3), S=Z_p[[t]]. Grouping even/odd powers proves the indicated embedding and finiteness; S is complete regular of dimension two, its fraction field agrees, and t^2 S is the conductor. The reduced conductor quotients are both Z_p. They have a nonempty centred boundary (the p-order ray), so infinite-conductor supports have not been discarded. N2 plus the normal-surface theorem proves CE for EVERY continuous signed obstacle here. Higher-dimensional positive/mixed-characteristic smooth source CE remains unproved by this argument.

For H=<2,3> there is a new explicit all-support example in EVERY dimension d>=2 and EVERY field, independent of any general source CE theorem. Use gauge a=(t^2,t^3,z_1,...,z_(d-1)), b=z_1+t and J=(b,t^2,z_2,...,z_(d-1)) in S. J is primary. By the homeomorphism define the continuous downstairs A(v)=w(J), where rho(w)=v, and obstacle f=-A. For integers m>=1 form the ACTUAL downstairs primary ideal
K_m=(b^m(z_1-mt), t^2 b^m, t^(2m+2))+(z_2,...,z_(d-1))^m.
When d=2 omit the last summand and put U=+infinity below. The first generator has no t-linear coefficient: m z_1^m-m z_1^m=0, including in characteristic dividing m. All its other t-degrees are zero or >=2, so it lies in R. The remaining generators lie there too. The radical contains t^2,t^3,z_1 and all the other z_j, hence K_m is proper primary. No generator is treated as a supplied executable expression.

Here is the universal bound, including EVERY support and infinite coordinate. Write s=w(t), u=w(z_1), B=w(b), U=min_(j>=2)w(z_j), so min(2s,u,U)=1 and A=min(B,2s,U). A is finite. Every displayed generator has value >=mA, hence w(K_m)>=mA. If U=A, the added ideal has value mU=mA, giving equality. Otherwise A<U. If 2s<=B, then s is finite and u=s: unequal values would force B=min(s,u)<2s. Since U>2s and min(2s,s,U)=1, s=u=1. The last original generator then has value mA+2. In the remaining case B<2s, A=B<U. If s<=u, then s is finite; B>=s. If s>1 all of 2s,u,U would exceed one, a contradiction. Thus s<=1, and t^2 b^m has value mA+2s<=mA+2. If s>u (including s=infinity), B=w(z_1-mt)=u: for m nonzero in k, m is a unit and the values are unequal, and if m=0 in k the second expression is simply z_1. The normalization and U>u give u=1, so the first generator has value mA+1. These cases exhaust all possibilities, including B=infinity, U=infinity, killed coordinates and cancellation. Consequently
0<=v(K_m)/m-A(v)<=2/m on the ENTIRE normalized boundary.

Therefore f is a uniform limit from below of -v(K_m)/m. Each profile is the evaluation of ACTUAL -E_(K_m)/m on ACTUAL Bl_(K_m)(R), negative effective and relatively ample, with positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve. Thus f belongs to independently geometric C even in higher positive characteristic where general CE is unknown. It is its own greatest C/D minorant. Since K_m subset A_m^R(f), the canonical profiles themselves obey the EVERY-degree uniform estimate 0<=p(f)-h_m^R(f)<=2/m. This establishes a quantitative geometric envelope across the infinite-conductor stratum without a conductor-value/N error or a root-map assumption.

In characteristic ZERO f is outside the ENTIRE finite REAL raw negative ideal cone Q_R, and its canonical algebra is NOT finitely generated. Define w_infinity by killing t,z_2,... and giving z_1 value one; define w_star by killing z_2,... and using monomial weights (t,b)=(1,2), with z_1=b-t. Both satisfy the chosen gauge, and A(w_infinity)=1, A(w_star)=2. For ANY proper primary downstairs ideal I, its image after killing the other z_j is primary in k[t^2,t^3,z_1]. Let e=w_infinity(I)>0. A generator attaining e has a unit denominator at both valuations. Its formal expansion has no t-degree-one terms, has nonzero z_1^e coefficient, and has zero t z_1^(e-1) coefficient. Its total-degree-e homogeneous part therefore cannot be a scalar multiple of b^e in characteristic zero. After z_1=b-t it contains some t^(e-j)b^j with j<e, of w_star-value e+j<=2e-1. Other total degrees cannot cancel this monomial. Thus w_star(I)<2w_infinity(I). Every nonzero finite nonnegative REAL combination of proper primary gauges preserves this strict inequality; unit terms vanish. A has equality, so A is outside the raw positive cone and f outside Q_R. Finite homogeneous generation of the canonical algebra would force a rational primary envelope by the elementary argument in n1, contradicting this separation. No claim of non-finite-generation in positive characteristic follows from the characteristic-zero argument.

This is continuous-envelope regularity WITH a canonical O(1/m) bound and WITHOUT canonical finite generation for an explicit cancellation-sensitive nonnormal higher-dimensional example. It is not a counterexample to CE, nor a raw geometric-core attainment claim. Under another gauge the same homogeneously transported obstacle keeps all canonical ideals, and the bound is divided by min v(new gauge)>0. G331's literal radial scope distinction, curve min(f,0), nilpotent reduction and empty dimension-zero case remain unchanged.

Own finite_diagnostics.py samples only its explicitly recorded rational weights, coherent cancellation cases and infinite-coordinate endpoints, and checks the t-linear cancellation exactly. Its output is finite diagnostic evidence, not the universal proof above. Artifacts n3.md, n3.tex, diagnostics-input.json and reports/finite-diagnostics.json; rerun python finite_diagnostics.py; python assemble.py; python verify.py.
